# 0020. Require high-assurance Phase 1 suite qualification

- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-20
- **Deciders:** Brian
- **Related:** M17; `docs/execution/phase1-suite-review.md`; v4 Part XXII Phase 1;
  R4 §§2, 8, 10, 11.6; ADR-0005; ADR-0013

## Context

M17 already requires a proposed Phase 1 suite, coverage matrices, mutation and
fuzz evidence, and two independent adversarial passes. Those nouns do not set a
qualification bar. A suite can claim each artifact while using trivial mutants,
short fuzz runs, shared oracles, vacuous predicates, or reviews that contaminate
one another.

Phase 1 will freeze foundations used by later parsers, graph projections,
recovery, revision tracking, and external adapters. Test quantity is therefore
not enough. Ratification needs evidence that the suite detects seeded defects,
survives malformed state, reproduces failures, and has no unexamined critical
requirement. The campaign must remain finite so it can be repeated after fixes.

## Decision

Phase 1 suite ratification SHALL use the **HAQP-1 high-assurance qualification
profile** below. Passing HAQP-1 does not ratify the suite; it only makes the
proposed packet eligible for Brian's separate T1 ratification decision.

### 1. Two execution lanes

- The **continuous lane** runs deterministic unit, integration, regression,
  malformed-input, and gate-canary tests on ordinary changes. It includes
  `just ci` and must not depend on elapsed-time fuzz success.
- The **qualification lane** runs from one fixed clean commit and source tree.
  It contains every HAQP-1 item and is rerun in full after the last verified
  defect is fixed. Partial reruns are diagnostic evidence only.
- Every command, exact toolchain and dependency version, lockfile hash, target,
  seed, declared non-locked regression/fuzz corpus hash, environment
  classification, exit status, and raw artifact hash is recorded. Missing
  evidence fails closed.

#### Qualification provenance amendment (2026-08-12)

The qualification packet is committed after its fixed-base campaign. Its
provenance records the campaign commit and that commit's tree hash. The
qualification commit MUST have exactly that campaign commit as its first
parent; the verifier checks parent and tree hashes, requires a clean tree, and
rejects any other provenance shape. This parent-binding design avoids a
self-referential packet commit hash while keeping evidence tied to one clean
source tree. No external manifest or signing key is required.

### 2. Bidirectional requirements traceability

- Every Phase 1 normative law, `MUST`, threat boundary, abuse case, fault class,
  work-order exit criterion, and ratification gate has a stable requirement ID.
- Every ID maps to at least one test, and every test maps back to at least one
  ID. Machine verification rejects duplicates, orphans, unknown IDs, and missing
  critical rows.
- Every applicable law has positive, negative, malformed/adversarial,
  basis/provenance, and deterministic-replay evidence. Stateful laws also have
  injected-fault and idempotent-recovery evidence.
- Uncovered critical rows cannot be waived inside the packet. Any exception is
  an exact coordinate accepted through a separate T1 amendment; wildcards,
  whole-file exclusions, and substring allowances are forbidden.

### 3. Tests of the tests

- Qualification predeclares at least **64 semantic mutants** across critical
  surfaces. Operators include predicate deletion/inversion, threshold ±1,
  missing enum or kind dispatch, success/error substitution, stale-Basis
  acceptance, wrong Holder/profile selection, skipped durable transition,
  disabled crash point, ordering nondeterminism, oracle short-circuit, and
  broadened allow-list.
- Every critical surface family receives at least eight mutants, and no single
  operator supplies more than one quarter of the denominator. Mutation selection
  cannot cluster around easy-to-kill utility paths.
- Mutation score is **100% of applicable, non-duplicate, non-equivalent
  mutants**. One survivor blocks eligibility.
- An equivalent or duplicate disposition names the mutant, shows the proof, and
  receives concurring verification in both adversarial-pass records. Disposed
  mutants remain visible in the numerator/denominator report.
- Every ratification gate and every M17 Level-3 measurement conjunct gets at
  least one disposable gate canary: a deliberate violation must make the exact
  expected gate fail. Canary execution occurs outside the working tree and
  restores the fixed review base afterward.

### 4. Generated, metamorphic, and fuzz evidence

- Five critical surface families each execute at least **100,000 accepted
  deterministic generated cases** from recorded seeds: source/CST/formatting,
  graph/interchange codecs, transforms/projections, repair/ILRP/recovery, and
  Basis/revision/query invalidation.
- Generator attempts and discards are recorded. Discard rate above one percent,
  post-failure filtering, or shrinking the declared domain fails qualification.
- Each family defines independent metamorphic relations where applicable:
  canonical reparse, idempotent replay, inverse/undo, irrelevant-input
  invariance, commuting independent transactions, incremental/full equivalence,
  and deterministic permutation. A relation is not proved by calling the
  implementation's own equality or normalization path on both sides.
- Each family also receives one **30-minute sanitizer-enabled fuzz campaign**
  with at least 16 predeclared seeds spanning valid, boundary, truncated,
  malformed, and hostile input. Total fuzz budget is at least 150 target-minutes.
- Every crash, panic, timeout, memory error, divergence, or minimized failure is
  a failing result. Minimized artifacts become named regression fixtures before
  the qualification lane is rerun.
- Concurrent code receives deterministic schedule exploration. If Phase 1 adds
  no concurrent implementation, the packet records the condition as not
  applicable rather than fabricating coverage.

### 5. Oracle and fault independence

- Incremental and full-reparse oracles may share raw bytes and published data
  schemas only. They may not share parser events, lowering code, canonicalizers,
  anchor recovery, comparison shortcuts, or expected-result construction.
- Expected values come from fixed literals, worked spec examples, or a separately
  implemented oracle. Self-snapshots generated by the system under test are not
  authority without independent verification.
- Every registered durable-transition crash boundary is injected immediately
  before and after the transition. Recovery runs twice and must reach the same
  terminal state without hidden staged data, duplicate effects, or mixed Basis.
- Fault matrix is exhaustive over registered boundaries. Runtime discovery and
  declared inventory must match exactly; either-side drift fails.

### 6. Independent adversarial review

- Pass 1 attacks implementation and packet for vacuity, shared-oracle coupling,
  missing negatives, weak mutants, fault omissions, nondeterminism, corpus
  leakage, exception broadening, and evidence/report drift.
- Pass 2 starts from the original spec and fixed review base. It cannot read Pass
  1 prompts, findings, dispositions, or fixes until it records its own findings.
- Passes use distinct reviewer identities and isolated conversation/session
  state. If both reviewers are automated, they use different model families;
  otherwise at least one reviewer is human. Sanitized prompt and reviewer
  identity hashes are recorded without credentials or secret material.
- Each pass records at least 12 concrete falsification attempts, including
  attempted violations that the suite correctly catches. Findings cite exact
  evidence and are independently reproduced before any fix.
- Zero verified findings may remain unresolved. False positives remain recorded
  with reproduction evidence; they are not silently deleted.

### 7. Bounded campaign and residual risk

- HAQP-1 qualification is a review-candidate campaign, not a per-edit tax. Its
  intended wall-clock ceiling is eight hours on the recorded reference machine.
  Crossing that ceiling twice blocks ratification and triggers a superseding ADR
  or harness optimization; thresholds cannot be silently reduced.
- Packet lists every known limitation with owner, severity, trigger, affected
  requirement, evidence, and planned resolution phase. "Future work" without
  those coordinates is invalid.
- Locked acceptance corpora remain black-box inputs touched only by existing
  approved verifiers. HAQP-1 does not authorize inspecting, listing, copying,
  hashing, or deriving new fixtures from locked corpus contents.

**What would falsify or reverse this:** two clean qualification attempts exceed
the eight-hour ceiling, required tooling cannot produce reproducible evidence,
or HAQP-1 encourages equivalent-mutant or low-value-case inflation without
finding real seeded defects. Reversal requires a superseding ADR with measured
campaign data and cannot weaken already-recorded failures or erase artifacts.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** ratification evidence demonstrates sensitivity, independence,
  replayability, traceability, and fault coverage instead of test count alone.
- **Negative:** final qualification consumes up to eight hours, requires at
  least 64 reviewed mutants and 150 target-minutes of fuzzing, and makes every
  post-campaign defect fix trigger another full run.
- **Follow-ups:** AM-17.1 binds M17's packet gate and review records to HAQP-1.
  Phase 1 work orders must budget both execution lanes without ratifying the
  suite automatically.

## Alternatives considered

- **Coverage percentages plus ordinary CI** — rejected because high line or
  branch coverage does not show that assertions detect semantic defects.
- **Unbounded fuzzing and exhaustive model checking** — rejected because results
  cannot be repeated on a review schedule and termination becomes subjective.
- **Broad source-wide mutation testing** — rejected because utility-code mutants
  inflate cost and score while diluting critical contract coverage.

# R-001 — a qualification stage may read the locked corpus; it may never write it

**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 1 at lane base `78c8f9b`, attempt A07
(corpus leakage): "stage remainder handling checks locked-corpus writes only,
so unauthorized read access remains accepted" — the same claim as F-44's
candidate option 3.

**Ruling (F-44, 2026-09-05, reaffirmed here).** For every stage's trace, a
write-class syscall on a path resolving under the repository's
`conformance/corpora` refuses unconditionally. Reads and stats are permitted:
the SLO graduation test measures the profile on the held-out corpus, which is
why it is held out, and git's index refresh and directory walkers touch every
tracked path. The carved fuzz binaries — the one process family whose evidence
is about the corpus — keep the full any-touch rule. The prohibition on
*tuning* against held-out data binds people and agents and is enforced by the
corpus manifest and its history, not by a stage trace.

**Effect.** A verified finding of class `corpus leakage` whose target file is
`crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs` and whose claim is that stage reads of the
locked corpus are accepted is cleared by this ruling while its status is `ruled` and the last commit
touching this file verifies against `conformance/haqp/ruling-signers`.

**Scope (added 2026-09-06 after A08 at lane `aa00d41`).** This ruling answers
only a claim whose prose contains `read access`. Matching on attack class and
target file alone cleared an unrelated finding in the same class and file; a
ruling answers a claim, not a coordinate.

**Scope narrowed again (2026-09-07, after A08 at lane `5fb1b57`).** A required
phrase can occur inside a sentence that negates it, so this ruling also lists
phrases whose presence means it does NOT answer the claim.

registered in `conformance/haqp/ruling-signers` was not loaded in the agent
until today, so the ruling was committed unsigned and cleared nothing in the
meantime. The commit carrying this line is the signed one, and `ruling_in_force`
reads the last commit to touch this file.

names a coordinate is now held to it rather than to the file, and no ruling may
clear more than one finding in a record: matching a second is evidence the
phrases are too broad, and the answer to that is a refusal.

**Narrowed again (2026-09-10, after A08 at lane `6b36bbb9`).** The ruling's own
text has always said the carved fuzz binaries keep the full any-touch rule, and
`claim_excludes` never encoded it — so the matcher would have cleared a finding
about a fuzz process reading the held-out corpus, which is leakage rather than a
stage read. `fuzz` is now an excluded phrase. The prose and the machine-readable
claim said different things for four days; the prose was right.

# R-003 — the verifier is not traced by itself

**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 2 at lane base `5fb1b57`, attempt A07 (corpus
leakage): "`verify_inventory_repo` does not run under strace and the corpus
access audit only covers the qualification lane stages, not the verifier
itself."

**True as stated.** The eight scope traces cover the lane's stages. The
verifier that judges those traces runs outside them.

**Ruling.** This is class C under AM-17.9: closing it requires the gate to be
its own adversary. Tracing the verifier under the lane's own tracer would
produce a trace the same verifier judges, so a verifier that wanted to hide a
locked-corpus read would simply not report it — the check would grow, the
assurance would not. The one-tracer constraint (F-43) also forbids nesting the
stage tracer inside itself.

What the campaign has instead is external: the verifier is tracked source at a
fixed commit, every change to it passes through a reviewed commit, and the
reviewers are given `haq.rs` in full precisely so a human-independent party
reads what the gate does. The residual — that a hostile author of the gate
could read the locked corpus from inside the gate — is stated, not closed.

**Effect.** A verified finding of class `corpus leakage` on
`crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs` whose claim is that the verifier is not
itself traced is cleared while this ruling's status is `ruled` and the last
commit touching this file verifies against `conformance/haqp/ruling-signers`.
It does not clear any claim about a stage trace, a directory fd, a `chdir`, or
a write to the locked corpus; those are excluded by name.

  1977	fn ordered_block_contents(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
  1978	    let mut anonymous = 0usize;
  1979	    let mut blocks = BTreeMap::new();
  1980	    for block in text.split("\n\n") {
  1981	        let marker = block
  1982	            .split_whitespace()
  1983	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  1984	            .map_or_else(
  1985	                || {
  1986	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  1987	                    anonymous += 1;
  1988	                    key
  1989	                },
  1990	                str::to_owned,
  1991	            );
  1992	        let tokens = block
  1993	            .split_whitespace()
  1994	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  1995	            .map(str::to_owned)
  1996	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  1997	        // Blocks containing only marker tokens carry no ordinary content whose
  1998	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  1999	        if !tokens.is_empty() {
  2000	            blocks.insert(marker, tokens);
  2001	        }
  2002	    }
  2003	    blocks
  2004	}

  1977	fn ordered_block_contents(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
  1978	    let mut anonymous = 0usize;
  1979	    let mut blocks = BTreeMap::new();
  1980	    for block in text.split("\n\n") {
  1981	        let marker = block
  1982	            .split_whitespace()
  1983	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  1984	            .map_or_else(
  1985	                || {
  1986	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  1987	                    anonymous += 1;
  1988	                    key
  1989	                },
  1990	                str::to_owned,
  1991	            );
  1992	        let tokens = block
  1993	            .split_whitespace()
  1994	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  1995	            .map(str::to_owned)
  1996	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  1997	        // Blocks containing only marker tokens carry no ordinary content whose
  1998	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  1999	        if !tokens.is_empty() {
  2000	            blocks.insert(marker, tokens);
  2001	        }
  2002	    }
  2003	    blocks
  2004	}

  1977	fn ordered_block_contents(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
  1978	    let mut anonymous = 0usize;
  1979	    let mut blocks = BTreeMap::new();
  1980	    for block in text.split("\n\n") {
  1981	        let marker = block
  1982	            .split_whitespace()
  1983	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  1984	            .map_or_else(
  1985	                || {
  1986	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  1987	                    anonymous += 1;
  1988	                    key
  1989	                },
  1990	                str::to_owned,
  1991	            );
  1992	        let tokens = block
  1993	            .split_whitespace()
  1994	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  1995	            .map(str::to_owned)
  1996	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  1997	        // Blocks containing only marker tokens carry no ordinary content whose
  1998	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  1999	        if !tokens.is_empty() {
  2000	            blocks.insert(marker, tokens);
  2001	        }
  2002	    }
  2003	    blocks
  2004	}

  6928	fn scope_trace_line_accesses(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool)> {

  6937	/// take no dirfd. Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10, A11): only `openat`'s FIRST
  6938	/// argument was read, so `renameat`'s destination dirfd was ignored and a
  6939	/// descriptor opened without `O_DIRECTORY` was dropped from the map entirely.
  6940	fn scope_trace_line_arguments(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool, Option<i64>)> {
  6941	    let Some((open, needle)) = FILE_SYSCALLS
  6942	        .into_iter()
  6943	        .filter_map(|needle| line.find(needle).map(|index| (index, needle)))
  6944	        .min_by_key(|(index, _)| *index)
  6945	    else {
  6946	        return Vec::new();
  6947	    };
  6948	    let rest = &line[open..];
  6949	    let write = WRITE_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  6950	        || (OPEN_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  6951	            && OPEN_WRITE_FLAGS.iter().any(|flag| rest.contains(flag)));

  6953	        2
  6954	    } else {
  6955	        1
  6956	    };

  6958	    // The argument list, past the syscall name: without this the text before a
  6959	    // path reads `openat(7`, whose last comma-separated piece is the name
  6960	    // glued to the fd and parses as nothing.
  6961	    let args = &rest[needle.len()..];
  6962	    let mut cursor = args;
  6963	    let mut consumed = 0usize;
  6964	    for _ in 0..wanted {
  6965	        let Some(start) = cursor.find('"') else { break };
  6966	        let Some(end) = cursor[start + 1..].find('"') else {
  6967	            break;
  6968	        };
  6969	        let dirfd = args[..consumed + start]
  6970	            .rsplit(',')
  6971	            .find_map(|argument| argument.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  6972	        out.push((cursor[start + 1..start + 1 + end].to_owned(), write, dirfd));
  6973	        consumed += start + 1 + end + 1;
  6974	        cursor = &cursor[start + 1 + end + 1..];
  6975	    }
  6976	    out
  6977	}

  7077	        && let Some(dir) = open_fds.get(&(pid, from)).cloned()
  7078	    {
  7079	        open_fds.insert((pid, to), dir);
  7080	    }

  7083	fn duplicated_fd(line: &str, returned_fd: Option<i64>) -> Option<(i64, i64)> {
  7084	    let to = returned_fd.filter(|fd| *fd >= 0)?;
  7085	    let call = ["dup(", "dup2(", "dup3(", "fcntl("]
  7086	        .into_iter()
  7087	        .find(|name| line.contains(name))?;
  7088	    if call == "fcntl(" && !line.contains("F_DUPFD") {
  7089	        return None;
  7090	    }
  7091	    // strace prints these as `dup2(3, 7) = 7` — integer arguments only, so the
  7092	    // first comma-separated piece is the source descriptor.
  7093	    let args = line.split_once(call)?.1;
  7094	    let from = args
  7095	        .split(',')
  7096	        .next()?
  7097	        .trim_end_matches(')')
  7098	        .trim()
  7099	        .parse::<i64>()
  7100	        .ok()?;
  7101	    Some((from, to))
  7102	}

  7104	fn record_chdir(
  7105	    line: &str,
  7106	    pid: u32,
  7107	    open_fds: &BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String>,
  7108	    cwds: &mut BTreeMap<u32, String>,
  7109	) {
  7110	    if !line.contains("chdir(") || !line.trim_end().ends_with("= 0") {
  7111	        return;
  7112	    }
  7113	    // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A07): `fchdir` was skipped, which left a STALE
  7114	    // cwd and unanchored every relative path after it. It names a directory by
  7115	    // fd, so the pid moves wherever that fd was opened; an fd this trace never
  7116	    // saw opened leaves the cwd UNKNOWN rather than stale.
  7117	    if line.contains("fchdir(") {
  7118	        let fd = line
  7119	            .split_once("fchdir(")
  7120	            .and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split(')').next())
  7121	            .and_then(|token| token.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7122	        match fd.and_then(|fd| open_fds.get(&(pid, fd))) {
  7123	            Some(dir) => cwds.insert(pid, dir.clone()),
  7124	            None => cwds.remove(&pid),
  7125	        };
  7126	        return;
  7127	    }
  7128	    let Some((target, _)) = scope_trace_line_accesses(line).first().cloned() else {
  7129	        return;
  7130	    };
  7131	    let resolved = if target.starts_with('/') {
  7132	        target
  7133	    } else {
  7134	        cwds.get(&pid)
  7135	            .map_or_else(|| target.clone(), |cwd| format!("{cwd}/{target}"))
  7136	    };
  7137	    cwds.insert(pid, resolved);
  7138	}

  7140	/// The path an fd-only write syscall on `line` names, resolved through the
  7141	/// descriptor map. Blind pass 1 at `ec045588` (A06): `chmod` names a path and
  7142	/// was listed; `fchmod` names a descriptor and was not, so changing the locked
  7143	/// corpus's mode through an open descriptor produced no write candidate.
  7144	fn fd_write_target(
  7145	    line: &str,
  7146	    pid: u32,
  7147	    open_fds: &BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String>,
  7148	) -> Option<String> {
  7149	    // Review of `f23bacd3`: a refused call changed nothing, and counting it
  7150	    // would refuse a trace for a write that never happened. Every syscall in
  7151	    // the table takes its descriptor first, which is what makes the first
  7152	    // argument the fd.
  7153	    if line.contains(" = -1 ") {
  7154	        return None;
  7155	    }
  7156	    let call = FD_WRITE_SYSCALLS
  7157	        .iter()
  7158	        .find(|call| line.contains(**call))?;
  7159	    let fd = line
  7160	        .split_once(*call)?
  7161	        .1
  7162	        .split([',', ')'])
  7163	        .next()?
  7164	        .trim()
  7165	        .parse::<i64>()
  7166	        .ok()?;
  7167	    open_fds.get(&(pid, fd)).cloned()
  7168	}

  7170	fn scan_scope_trace<R: std::io::BufRead>(mut reader: R) -> Result<ScopeTraceScan> {
  7171	    let mut scan = ScopeTraceScan::default();
  7172	    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
  7173	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
  7174	    // Blind pass 1 at f360e90 (A07): `openat(AT_FDCWD, ".../heldout", O_DIRECTORY) = 7`
  7175	    // followed by `openat(7, "x.md", O_WRONLY)` named the locked corpus only on
  7176	    // the permitted read; the write carried no fragment. Directory fds are
  7177	    // remembered per pid from their open's return value, and a path relative
  7178	    // to one is judged under that directory. An `<unfinished ...>` open is
  7179	    // completed by its `<... openat resumed>) = fd` line.
  7180	    let mut open_fds: BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7181	    let mut unfinished: BTreeMap<u32, (String, bool)> = BTreeMap::new();
  7182	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A07): a `chdir` into the locked corpus made
  7183	    // every later relative write nameless — no fragment, and resolution
  7184	    // against the repository root put it somewhere harmless. The cwd each pid
  7185	    // announces is remembered, and its relative paths resolve there.
  7186	    let mut cwds: BTreeMap<u32, String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7187	    loop {
  7188	        buf.clear();
  7189	        if reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)? == 0 {
  7190	            break;
  7191	        }
  7192	        hasher.update(&buf);
  7193	        // Exactly `str::lines`: one trailing `\n`, then one `\r`, stripped.
  7194	        let line = buf.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(&buf);
  7195	        let line = line.strip_suffix(b"\r").unwrap_or(line);
  7196	        let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(line);
  7197	        if scan.forbidden.is_none() {
  7198	            let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7199	            scan.forbidden = FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS
  7200	                .into_iter()
  7201	                .find(|fragment| lower.contains(fragment));
  7202	        }
  7203	        let mut tokens = line.splitn(2, ' ');
  7204	        if let Some(pid) = tokens.next().and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok()) {
  7205	            scan.pids.insert(pid);
  7206	            if tokens.next() == Some("+++ exited with 0 +++") {
  7207	                scan.exited_zero.insert(pid);
  7208	            }
  7209	            // A pid that exited holds no directory fds; a later process
  7210	            // reusing the number must not inherit them.
  7211	            if line.contains(" +++ exited with ") || line.contains(" +++ killed by ") {
  7212	                open_fds.retain(|(owner, _), _| *owner != pid);
  7213	            }
  7214	        }
  7215	        let pid = line
  7216	            .split(' ')
  7217	            .next()
  7218	            .and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok());
  7219	        let returned_fd = line
  7220	            .rsplit(" = ")
  7221	            .next()
  7222	            .and_then(|tail| tail.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7223	        if let (Some(pid), true) = (pid, line.contains("<... openat resumed>"))
  7224	            && let (Some((path, is_dir)), Some(fd)) = (unfinished.remove(&pid), returned_fd)
  7225	        {
  7226	            if is_dir && fd >= 0 {
  7227	                open_fds.insert((pid, fd), path);
  7228	            } else {
  7229	                open_fds.remove(&(pid, fd));
  7230	            }
  7231	        }
  7232	        // Parsed ONCE and carried: `anchor_relative_paths` used to re-parse the
  7233	        // line and zip positionally against this vector, which is only safe
  7234	        // while the two parses agree on how many entries they yield (review of
  7235	        // `7e4ba39`). Passing the dirfds through removes the coupling.
  7236	        let mut arguments = scope_trace_line_arguments(&line);
  7237	        if let Some(pid) = pid {
  7238	            anchor_relative_paths(pid, &open_fds, &cwds, &mut arguments);
  7239	        }
  7240	        let mut accesses = arguments
  7241	            .into_iter()
  7242	            .map(|(path, write, _)| (path, write))
  7243	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7244	        // Blind pass 1 at `ec045588` (A06): `chmod` and `fchmodat` name a
  7245	        // path and were listed; `fchmod` names a descriptor and was not, so
  7246	        // changing the locked corpus's mode or owner through an open
  7247	        // descriptor produced no write candidate at all. Every successful
  7248	        // open's path is already remembered for its fd, so the descriptor
  7249	        // resolves to the file it names.
  7250	        if let Some(pid) = pid
  7251	            && let Some(path) = fd_write_target(&line, pid, &open_fds)
  7252	        {
  7253	            accesses.push((path, true));
  7254	        }
  7255	        if let Some(pid) = pid {
  7256	            // Blind pass 1 at e09ae5e (A07): the cwd and dirfd maps are keyed
  7257	            // per pid and were never inherited, so a parent that chdir'd into
  7258	            // the locked corpus and then forked left the CHILD unanchored —
  7259	            // its relative write carried no forbidden text and resolved
  7260	            // against nothing. A child begins life with its parent's working
  7261	            // directory and its open descriptors.
  7262	            if let Some(child) = clone_child_pid(&line) {
  7263	                if let Some(cwd) = cwds.get(&pid).cloned() {
  7264	                    cwds.insert(child, cwd);
  7265	                }
  7266	                let inherited = open_fds
  7267	                    .range((pid, i64::MIN)..=(pid, i64::MAX))
  7268	                    .map(|((_, fd), dir)| (*fd, dir.clone()))
  7269	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7270	                for (fd, dir) in inherited {
  7271	                    open_fds.insert((child, fd), dir);
  7272	                }
  7273	            }
  7274	            record_chdir(&line, pid, &open_fds, &mut cwds);
  7275	            record_duplicated_fd(&line, pid, returned_fd, &mut open_fds);
  7276	            // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10): only `O_DIRECTORY` opens were
  7277	            // remembered, so a descriptor opened without it and later used as
  7278	            // a dirfd resolved against nothing. Every successful open's path
  7279	            // is remembered for its fd; one that is not a directory simply
  7280	            // never appears as a dirfd.
  7281	            if (line.contains("openat(") || line.contains("openat2(") || line.contains(" open("))
  7282	                && let Some((path, _)) = accesses.first()
  7283	            {
  7284	                if line.contains("<unfinished ...>") {
  7285	                    unfinished.insert(pid, (path.clone(), true));
  7286	                } else if let Some(fd) = returned_fd {
  7287	                    if fd >= 0 {
  7288	                        open_fds.insert((pid, fd), path.clone());
  7289	                    } else {
  7290	                        open_fds.remove(&(pid, fd));
  7291	                    }
  7292	                }
  7293	            }
  7294	        }
  7295	        for (path, write) in accesses {
  7296	            // Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A02): candidates were collected only
  7297	            // when the path LOOKED like the corpus, so F-64's inode comparison
  7298	            // — added for exactly the case where it does not — never saw a
  7299	            // hard link under an unrelated name. Every write is a candidate;
  7300	            // the lexical rules still decide the lexical cases, and identity
  7301	            // decides the rest.
  7302	            if write {
  7303	                scan.locked_write_candidates.push(path.clone());
  7304	            }
  7305	            scan.open_paths.insert(path);
  7306	        }
  7307	    }
  7308	    scan.raw_blake3 = hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string();
  7309	    Ok(scan)
  7310	}

  7325	/// F-44 ruling (Brian, 2026-09-05). A stage may READ the locked corpus -- the
  7340	/// Identity is read from directory metadata; no corpus file is opened.
  7341	fn locked_corpus_identities(root: &Utf8Path, within: &str) -> Result<BTreeSet<(u64, u64)>> {
  7342	    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  7343	    let corpora = root.join(within);
  7344	    let mut identities = BTreeSet::new();
  7345	    if !corpora.is_dir() {
  7346	        return Ok(identities);
  7347	    }
  7348	    let mut stack = vec![corpora];
  7349	    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
  7350	        // Review of `bba803d4`: skipping an unreadable directory returned a
  7351	        // partial set, and a hard link to a file inside it would then pass. A
  7352	        // corpus this cannot enumerate is a corpus it cannot protect.
  7353	        let entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
  7354	            .with_context(|| format!("enumerate the locked corpus at {dir}"))?;
  7355	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
  7356	            let path = entry.path();
  7357	            let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
  7358	                .with_context(|| format!("stat {} in the locked corpus", path.display()))?;
  7359	            if metadata.is_dir() {
  7360	                if let Ok(dir) = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path) {
  7361	                    stack.push(dir);
  7362	                }
  7363	            } else if metadata.is_file() {
  7364	                identities.insert((metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));
  7365	            }
  7366	        }
  7367	    }
  7368	    Ok(identities)
  7369	}

  7371	fn locked_corpus_write(
  7372	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7373	    candidates: &[String],
  7374	    label: &str,
  7375	) -> Result<Option<String>> {
  7376	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  7377	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  7378	    let identities = locked_corpus_identities(root, "conformance/corpora")?;
  7379	    for lexical in candidates {
  7380	        let path = Path::new(lexical);
  7381	        // Blind pass 1 at 78c8f9b (A12): a relative write from a subdirectory,
  7382	        // `../conformance/corpora/heldout/x`, joined onto the root climbed out
  7383	        // of it and passed. The cwd is not receipted, so a relative write that
  7384	        // names the locked corpus at all is refused, before any resolution.
  7385	        let lower = lexical.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7386	        if !path.is_absolute()
  7387	            && (lower.contains("conformance/corpora/") || lower.ends_with("conformance/corpora"))
  7388	        {
  7389	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  7390	        }
  7391	        let local = if path.is_absolute() {
  7392	            path.to_path_buf()
  7393	        } else {
  7394	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  7395	        };
  7396	        // A path that no longer resolves (deleted after the trace) is judged
  7397	        // lexically: the conservative direction, since a lexical
  7398	        // conformance/corpora prefix still refuses.
  7399	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(&local).unwrap_or(local);
  7400	        if let Ok(relative) = canonical.strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  7401	            && relative
  7402	                .to_string_lossy()
  7403	                .to_ascii_lowercase()
  7404	                .starts_with("conformance/corpora")
  7405	        {
  7406	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  7407	        }
  7408	        // A07: a hard link is a second name for the same inode, so no amount
  7409	        // of path reasoning sees it. Identity does.
  7410	        if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&canonical) {
  7411	            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  7412	            if identities.contains(&(metadata.dev(), metadata.ino())) {
  7413	                return Ok(Some(format!(
  7414	                    "{lexical} (hard link into the locked corpus)"
  7415	                )));
  7416	            }
  7417	        }
  7418	    }
  7419	    Ok(None)
  7420	}

  7449	            std::path::PathBuf::from(path)
  7450	        } else {
  7451	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  7452	        };

  7463	fn scan_scope_trace_union(
  7464	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7465	    row: &CorpusScopeTrace,
  7466	) -> Result<(ScopeTraceScan, BTreeSet<String>, Option<&'static str>)> {

  7469	    let remainder = scan_scope_trace_file(&remainder_path, &label)?;

  7472	    // (F-44). Parts are the fuzz binaries: any fragment refuses.
  7473	    let mut forbidden = None;
  7474	    for part in &row.parts {
  7475	        let part_path = safe_repo_path(root, &part.trace, "corpus scope trace part")?;
  7476	        let scan = scan_scope_trace_file(&part_path, &label)?;
  7477	        require_eq(
  7478	            &format!(
  7479	                "{} corpus scope part {} trace_blake3",
  7480	                row.scope, part.trace
  7481	            ),
  7482	            &part.trace_blake3,
  7483	            &scan.raw_blake3,
  7484	        )?;
  7485	        forbidden = forbidden.or(scan.forbidden);
  7486	        // Blind pass 1 at `0a0b4b4b` (A07): the any-touch rule fired on the
  7487	        // lexical fragments `heldout` and `conformance/corpora`, so a hard
  7488	        // link under any other name was invisible — and F-64's inode
  7489	        // comparison guarded writes only, while the carved fuzz binaries are
  7490	        // the one family for which a READ is the leak. Identity applies to
  7491	        // every path a fuzz part opened.
  7492	        if forbidden.is_none() && corpus_identity_touched(root, &scan.open_paths)? {
  7493	            forbidden = Some("locked corpus reached by inode identity");
  7494	        }
  7495	        open.extend(scan.open_paths);
  7496	    }
  7497	    Ok((remainder, open, forbidden))
  7498	}

  7545	/// Resolve corpus paths from raw strace metadata. Lexical path filtering alone

  7614	    lexical_lower: &str,
  7615	    locked: LockedCorpus,

  7619	        return Ok(false);
  7620	    }

  7632	fn resolved_corpus_paths_digest_from(
  7633	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7634	    trace_root: &str,
  7635	    open_paths: &BTreeSet<String>,
  7636	    label: &str,
  7637	    access: CorpusAccess,
  7638	    locked: LockedCorpus,
  7639	) -> Result<String> {
  7640	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  7641	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  7642	    let trace_root = Path::new(trace_root);
  7643	    anyhow::ensure!(
  7644	        trace_root.is_absolute(),
  7645	        "{label}: trace_root must be absolute"
  7646	    );
  7647	    let mut resolved = BTreeSet::new();
  7648	    for lexical in open_paths {
  7649	        let lexical_path = Path::new(&lexical);
  7650	        let lexical_lower = lexical_path.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase();
  7651	        if relative_trace_path_is_skipped(lexical_path, &lexical_lower, locked, label)? {
  7652	            continue;
  7653	        }
  7654	        let under_trace_root =
  7655	            !lexical_path.is_absolute() || lexical_path.strip_prefix(trace_root).is_ok();
  7656	        if !under_trace_root {
  7657	            continue;
  7658	        }
  7659	        let local = trace_path_to_repo(root, trace_root, lexical)
  7660	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: cannot map traced repository path"))?;
  7661	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(local.as_std_path())
  7662	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path cannot be resolved"))?;
  7663	        let relative = canonical
  7664	            .strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  7665	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path escapes repository root"))?;
  7666	        let relative = relative.to_str().context("non-UTF-8 traced corpus path")?;
  7667	        let lower = relative.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7668	        if locked == LockedCorpus::AnyTouch {
  7669	            for forbidden in FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS {
  7670	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7671	                    !lower.contains(forbidden),
  7672	                    "{label}: traced repository path resolves into forbidden data"
  7673	                );
  7674	            }
  7675	        }
  7676	        if lexical_lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  7677	            || lexical_lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  7678	            || lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  7679	            || lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  7680	        {
  7681	            resolved.insert(format!("{lexical}\0{relative}"));
  7682	        }
  7683	    }
  7684	    if access == CorpusAccess::Required {
  7685	        anyhow::ensure!(
  7686	            !resolved.is_empty(),
  7687	            "{label}: trace contains no resolvable fuzz corpus path"
  7688	        );
  7689	    }
  7690	    let resolved = resolved.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7691	    let resolved_bytes = format!("{}\n", resolved.join("\n"));
  7692	    Ok(blake3::hash(resolved_bytes.as_bytes()).to_hex().to_string())
  7693	}

  7695	/// Canonicalize the existing prefix of a traced path, then append historical
  7696	/// leaf components that libFuzzer may have deleted after opening them. This
  7697	/// preserves symlink and root-boundary checks without requiring every path in
  7698	/// a long-running trace to remain present at receipt time.
  7699	fn canonicalize_trace_path(path: &Path) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
  7700	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
  7701	    let mut cursor = path;
  7702	    loop {
  7703	        match fs::symlink_metadata(cursor) {
  7704	            Ok(_) => break,
  7705	            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
  7706	                missing.push(
  7707	                    cursor
  7708	                        .file_name()
  7709	                        .context("traced path has no recoverable leaf")?
  7710	                        .to_owned(),
  7711	                );
  7712	                let leaf = missing.last().expect("just pushed missing leaf");
  7713	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7714	                    leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".") && leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".."),
  7715	                    "traced path contains a parent-directory suffix"
  7716	                );
  7717	                cursor = cursor
  7718	                    .parent()
  7719	                    .context("traced path has no existing ancestor")?;
  7720	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7721	                    cursor.file_name() != Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("corpus")),
  7722	                    "traced path is missing a corpus entry; symlink history is unavailable"
  7723	                );
  7724	            }
  7725	            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
  7726	        }
  7727	    }
  7728	    let mut canonical = fs::canonicalize(cursor)?;
  7729	    for component in missing.into_iter().rev() {
  7730	        canonical.push(component);
  7731	    }
  7732	    Ok(canonical)
  7733	}

  7735	fn trace_path_to_repo(root: &Utf8Path, trace_root: &Path, lexical: &str) -> Result<Utf8PathBuf> {
  7736	    let path = Path::new(lexical);
  7737	    if path.is_absolute() {
  7738	        if let Ok(relative) = path.strip_prefix(trace_root) {
  7739	            return Ok(
  7740	                root.join(Utf8Path::from_path(relative).context("non-UTF-8 traced relative path")?)
  7741	            );
  7742	        }
  7743	        anyhow::bail!("absolute traced path is outside recorded trace root")
  7744	    }
  7745	    Ok(root.join(Utf8Path::from_path(path).context("non-UTF-8 traced relative path")?))
  7746	}

  7170	fn scan_scope_trace<R: std::io::BufRead>(mut reader: R) -> Result<ScopeTraceScan> {

  7173	    let mut buf = Vec::new();

  7175	    // followed by `openat(7, "x.md", O_WRONLY)` named the locked corpus only on
  7176	    // the permitted read; the write carried no fragment. Directory fds are
  7177	    // remembered per pid from their open's return value, and a path relative
  7178	    // to one is judged under that directory. An `<unfinished ...>` open is
  7179	    // completed by its `<... openat resumed>) = fd` line.
  7180	    let mut open_fds: BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7181	    let mut unfinished: BTreeMap<u32, (String, bool)> = BTreeMap::new();
  7182	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A07): a `chdir` into the locked corpus made
  7183	    // every later relative write nameless — no fragment, and resolution
  7184	    // against the repository root put it somewhere harmless. The cwd each pid
  7185	    // announces is remembered, and its relative paths resolve there.
  7186	    let mut cwds: BTreeMap<u32, String> = BTreeMap::new();
  7187	    loop {
  7188	        buf.clear();
  7189	        if reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)? == 0 {
  7190	            break;
  7191	        }
  7192	        hasher.update(&buf);
  7193	        // Exactly `str::lines`: one trailing `\n`, then one `\r`, stripped.
  7194	        let line = buf.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(&buf);
  7195	        let line = line.strip_suffix(b"\r").unwrap_or(line);
  7196	        let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(line);
  7197	        if scan.forbidden.is_none() {
  7198	            let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7199	            scan.forbidden = FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS
  7200	                .into_iter()
  7201	                .find(|fragment| lower.contains(fragment));
  7202	        }
  7203	        let mut tokens = line.splitn(2, ' ');
  7204	        if let Some(pid) = tokens.next().and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok()) {
  7205	            scan.pids.insert(pid);
  7206	            if tokens.next() == Some("+++ exited with 0 +++") {
  7207	                scan.exited_zero.insert(pid);
  7208	            }

  7210	            // reusing the number must not inherit them.
  7211	            if line.contains(" +++ exited with ") || line.contains(" +++ killed by ") {
  7212	                open_fds.retain(|(owner, _), _| *owner != pid);
  7213	            }
  7214	        }

  7216	            .split(' ')
  7217	            .next()
  7218	            .and_then(|token| token.parse::<u32>().ok());

  7220	            .rsplit(" = ")
  7221	            .next()
  7222	            .and_then(|tail| tail.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7223	        if let (Some(pid), true) = (pid, line.contains("<... openat resumed>"))
  7224	            && let (Some((path, is_dir)), Some(fd)) = (unfinished.remove(&pid), returned_fd)
  7225	        {
  7226	            if is_dir && fd >= 0 {
  7227	                open_fds.insert((pid, fd), path);
  7228	            } else {
  7229	                open_fds.remove(&(pid, fd));
  7230	            }
  7231	        }
  7232	        // Parsed ONCE and carried: `anchor_relative_paths` used to re-parse the
  7233	        // line and zip positionally against this vector, which is only safe
  7234	        // while the two parses agree on how many entries they yield (review of
  7235	        // `7e4ba39`). Passing the dirfds through removes the coupling.
  7236	        let mut arguments = scope_trace_line_arguments(&line);
  7237	        if let Some(pid) = pid {
  7238	            anchor_relative_paths(pid, &open_fds, &cwds, &mut arguments);
  7239	        }
  7240	        let mut accesses = arguments
  7241	            .into_iter()
  7242	            .map(|(path, write, _)| (path, write))
  7243	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7244	        // Blind pass 1 at `ec045588` (A06): `chmod` and `fchmodat` name a
  7245	        // path and were listed; `fchmod` names a descriptor and was not, so
  7246	        // changing the locked corpus's mode or owner through an open
  7247	        // descriptor produced no write candidate at all. Every successful
  7248	        // open's path is already remembered for its fd, so the descriptor
  7249	        // resolves to the file it names.
  7250	        if let Some(pid) = pid
  7251	            && let Some(path) = fd_write_target(&line, pid, &open_fds)
  7252	        {
  7253	            accesses.push((path, true));
  7254	        }
  7255	        if let Some(pid) = pid {
  7256	            // Blind pass 1 at e09ae5e (A07): the cwd and dirfd maps are keyed
  7257	            // per pid and were never inherited, so a parent that chdir'd into
  7258	            // the locked corpus and then forked left the CHILD unanchored —
  7259	            // its relative write carried no forbidden text and resolved
  7260	            // against nothing. A child begins life with its parent's working
  7261	            // directory and its open descriptors.
  7262	            if let Some(child) = clone_child_pid(&line) {
  7263	                if let Some(cwd) = cwds.get(&pid).cloned() {
  7264	                    cwds.insert(child, cwd);
  7265	                }
  7266	                let inherited = open_fds
  7267	                    .range((pid, i64::MIN)..=(pid, i64::MAX))
  7268	                    .map(|((_, fd), dir)| (*fd, dir.clone()))
  7269	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7270	                for (fd, dir) in inherited {
  7271	                    open_fds.insert((child, fd), dir);
  7272	                }
  7273	            }
  7274	            record_chdir(&line, pid, &open_fds, &mut cwds);
  7275	            record_duplicated_fd(&line, pid, returned_fd, &mut open_fds);
  7276	            // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10): only `O_DIRECTORY` opens were
  7277	            // remembered, so a descriptor opened without it and later used as
  7278	            // a dirfd resolved against nothing. Every successful open's path
  7279	            // is remembered for its fd; one that is not a directory simply
  7280	            // never appears as a dirfd.
  7281	            if (line.contains("openat(") || line.contains("openat2(") || line.contains(" open("))
  7282	                && let Some((path, _)) = accesses.first()
  7283	            {
  7284	                if line.contains("<unfinished ...>") {
  7285	                    unfinished.insert(pid, (path.clone(), true));
  7286	                } else if let Some(fd) = returned_fd {
  7287	                    if fd >= 0 {
  7288	                        open_fds.insert((pid, fd), path.clone());
  7289	                    } else {
  7290	                        open_fds.remove(&(pid, fd));
  7291	                    }
  7292	                }
  7293	            }
  7294	        }
  7295	        for (path, write) in accesses {
  7296	            // Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A02): candidates were collected only
  7297	            // when the path LOOKED like the corpus, so F-64's inode comparison
  7298	            // — added for exactly the case where it does not — never saw a
  7299	            // hard link under an unrelated name. Every write is a candidate;
  7300	            // the lexical rules still decide the lexical cases, and identity
  7301	            // decides the rest.
  7302	            if write {
  7303	                scan.locked_write_candidates.push(path.clone());
  7304	            }
  7305	            scan.open_paths.insert(path);
  7306	        }
  7307	    }
  7308	    scan.raw_blake3 = hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string();
  7309	    Ok(scan)
  7310	}

  7325	/// F-44 ruling (Brian, 2026-09-05). A stage may READ the locked corpus -- the
  7340	/// Identity is read from directory metadata; no corpus file is opened.
  7341	fn locked_corpus_identities(root: &Utf8Path, within: &str) -> Result<BTreeSet<(u64, u64)>> {
  7342	    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  7343	    let corpora = root.join(within);
  7344	    let mut identities = BTreeSet::new();
  7345	    if !corpora.is_dir() {
  7346	        return Ok(identities);
  7347	    }
  7348	    let mut stack = vec![corpora];
  7349	    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
  7350	        // Review of `bba803d4`: skipping an unreadable directory returned a
  7351	        // partial set, and a hard link to a file inside it would then pass. A
  7352	        // corpus this cannot enumerate is a corpus it cannot protect.
  7353	        let entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
  7354	            .with_context(|| format!("enumerate the locked corpus at {dir}"))?;
  7355	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
  7356	            let path = entry.path();
  7357	            let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
  7358	                .with_context(|| format!("stat {} in the locked corpus", path.display()))?;
  7359	            if metadata.is_dir() {
  7360	                if let Ok(dir) = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path) {
  7361	                    stack.push(dir);
  7362	                }
  7363	            } else if metadata.is_file() {
  7364	                identities.insert((metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()));
  7365	            }
  7366	        }
  7367	    }
  7368	    Ok(identities)
  7369	}

  7371	fn locked_corpus_write(
  7372	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7373	    candidates: &[String],
  7374	    label: &str,
  7375	) -> Result<Option<String>> {
  7376	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  7377	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  7378	    let identities = locked_corpus_identities(root, "conformance/corpora")?;
  7379	    for lexical in candidates {
  7380	        let path = Path::new(lexical);
  7381	        // Blind pass 1 at 78c8f9b (A12): a relative write from a subdirectory,
  7382	        // `../conformance/corpora/heldout/x`, joined onto the root climbed out
  7383	        // of it and passed. The cwd is not receipted, so a relative write that
  7384	        // names the locked corpus at all is refused, before any resolution.
  7385	        let lower = lexical.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7386	        if !path.is_absolute()
  7387	            && (lower.contains("conformance/corpora/") || lower.ends_with("conformance/corpora"))
  7388	        {
  7389	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  7390	        }
  7391	        let local = if path.is_absolute() {
  7392	            path.to_path_buf()
  7393	        } else {
  7394	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  7395	        };
  7396	        // A path that no longer resolves (deleted after the trace) is judged
  7397	        // lexically: the conservative direction, since a lexical
  7398	        // conformance/corpora prefix still refuses.
  7399	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(&local).unwrap_or(local);
  7400	        if let Ok(relative) = canonical.strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  7401	            && relative
  7402	                .to_string_lossy()
  7403	                .to_ascii_lowercase()
  7404	                .starts_with("conformance/corpora")
  7405	        {
  7406	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  7407	        }
  7408	        // A07: a hard link is a second name for the same inode, so no amount
  7409	        // of path reasoning sees it. Identity does.
  7410	        if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&canonical) {
  7411	            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  7412	            if identities.contains(&(metadata.dev(), metadata.ino())) {
  7413	                return Ok(Some(format!(
  7414	                    "{lexical} (hard link into the locked corpus)"
  7415	                )));
  7416	            }
  7417	        }
  7418	    }
  7419	    Ok(None)
  7420	}

  7436	/// Scan a scope's stored remainder and every carved part, binding each part's
  7437	/// bytes to the digest the row declares. Returns the remainder's scan and the
  7438	/// union of open paths; a locked-corpus fragment in ANY file is the row's.
  7439	/// Whether any of `paths` names a file the locked corpus also names. A hard
  7440	/// link is a second name for one inode, so no amount of path reasoning sees it.
  7441	fn corpus_identity_touched(root: &Utf8Path, paths: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Result<bool> {
  7442	    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  7443	    let identities = locked_corpus_identities(root, "conformance/corpora")?;
  7444	    if identities.is_empty() {
  7445	        return Ok(false);
  7446	    }
  7447	    for path in paths {
  7448	        let local = if Path::new(path).is_absolute() {
  7449	            std::path::PathBuf::from(path)
  7450	        } else {
  7451	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  7452	        };
  7453	        let resolved = canonicalize_trace_path(&local).unwrap_or(local);
  7454	        if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&resolved)
  7455	            && identities.contains(&(metadata.dev(), metadata.ino()))
  7456	        {
  7457	            return Ok(true);
  7458	        }
  7459	    }
  7460	    Ok(false)
  7461	}

  7463	fn scan_scope_trace_union(
  7464	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7465	    row: &CorpusScopeTrace,
  7466	) -> Result<(ScopeTraceScan, BTreeSet<String>, Option<&'static str>)> {
  7467	    let label = format!("{} corpus scope", row.scope);
  7468	    let remainder_path = safe_repo_path(root, &row.trace, "corpus scope trace")?;
  7469	    let remainder = scan_scope_trace_file(&remainder_path, &label)?;
  7470	    let mut open = remainder.open_paths.clone();
  7471	    // The remainder is a stage: reads permitted, writes judged by the caller
  7472	    // (F-44). Parts are the fuzz binaries: any fragment refuses.
  7473	    let mut forbidden = None;
  7474	    for part in &row.parts {
  7475	        let part_path = safe_repo_path(root, &part.trace, "corpus scope trace part")?;
  7476	        let scan = scan_scope_trace_file(&part_path, &label)?;
  7477	        require_eq(
  7478	            &format!(
  7479	                "{} corpus scope part {} trace_blake3",
  7480	                row.scope, part.trace
  7481	            ),
  7482	            &part.trace_blake3,
  7483	            &scan.raw_blake3,
  7484	        )?;
  7485	        forbidden = forbidden.or(scan.forbidden);
  7486	        // Blind pass 1 at `0a0b4b4b` (A07): the any-touch rule fired on the
  7487	        // lexical fragments `heldout` and `conformance/corpora`, so a hard
  7488	        // link under any other name was invisible — and F-64's inode
  7489	        // comparison guarded writes only, while the carved fuzz binaries are
  7490	        // the one family for which a READ is the leak. Identity applies to
  7491	        // every path a fuzz part opened.
  7492	        if forbidden.is_none() && corpus_identity_touched(root, &scan.open_paths)? {
  7493	            forbidden = Some("locked corpus reached by inode identity");
  7494	        }
  7495	        open.extend(scan.open_paths);
  7496	    }
  7497	    Ok((remainder, open, forbidden))
  7498	}

  7600	/// Whether a relative traced path is left out of corpus resolution.
  7601	///
  7602	/// Relative paths are interpreted against the process cwd or a directory fd,
  7603	/// which the trace does not receipt; resolving one as root-relative can hide a
  7604	/// locked corpus behind a chdir or alias. A fuzz binary is invoked with an
  7605	/// absolute corpus path, so a relative one is the campaign's defect and refuses
  7606	/// (`AnyTouch`). A stage's helpers name seeds relative to their cwd (git's
  7607	/// index refresh, the campaign's seed manifest) and reviewer tooling opens
  7608	/// `../nvidia0` under /dev: unresolvable, and able to add no corpus entry, so
  7609	/// under `WritesOnly` every relative path is skipped rather than refused as an
  7610	/// escape (F-44). Writes were already judged root-relative by
  7611	/// `locked_corpus_write`.
  7612	fn relative_trace_path_is_skipped(
  7613	    lexical_path: &Path,
  7614	    lexical_lower: &str,
  7615	    locked: LockedCorpus,
  7616	    label: &str,
  7617	) -> Result<bool> {
  7618	    if lexical_path.is_absolute() {
  7619	        return Ok(false);
  7620	    }
  7621	    let names_corpus =
  7622	        lexical_lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/") || lexical_lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/");
  7623	    match locked {
  7624	        LockedCorpus::AnyTouch if names_corpus => anyhow::bail!(
  7625	            "{label}: relative fuzz corpus path lacks authenticated cwd/dirfd binding"
  7626	        ),
  7627	        LockedCorpus::AnyTouch => Ok(false),
  7628	        LockedCorpus::WritesOnly => Ok(true),
  7629	    }
  7630	}

  7632	fn resolved_corpus_paths_digest_from(
  7633	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7634	    trace_root: &str,
  7635	    open_paths: &BTreeSet<String>,
  7636	    label: &str,
  7637	    access: CorpusAccess,
  7638	    locked: LockedCorpus,
  7639	) -> Result<String> {
  7640	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  7641	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  7642	    let trace_root = Path::new(trace_root);
  7643	    anyhow::ensure!(
  7644	        trace_root.is_absolute(),
  7645	        "{label}: trace_root must be absolute"
  7646	    );
  7647	    let mut resolved = BTreeSet::new();
  7648	    for lexical in open_paths {
  7649	        let lexical_path = Path::new(&lexical);
  7650	        let lexical_lower = lexical_path.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase();
  7651	        if relative_trace_path_is_skipped(lexical_path, &lexical_lower, locked, label)? {
  7652	            continue;
  7653	        }
  7654	        let under_trace_root =
  7655	            !lexical_path.is_absolute() || lexical_path.strip_prefix(trace_root).is_ok();
  7656	        if !under_trace_root {
  7657	            continue;
  7658	        }
  7659	        let local = trace_path_to_repo(root, trace_root, lexical)
  7660	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: cannot map traced repository path"))?;
  7661	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(local.as_std_path())
  7662	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path cannot be resolved"))?;
  7663	        let relative = canonical
  7664	            .strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  7665	            .with_context(|| format!("{label}: traced repository path escapes repository root"))?;
  7666	        let relative = relative.to_str().context("non-UTF-8 traced corpus path")?;
  7667	        let lower = relative.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7668	        if locked == LockedCorpus::AnyTouch {
  7669	            for forbidden in FORBIDDEN_TRACE_FRAGMENTS {
  7670	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7671	                    !lower.contains(forbidden),
  7672	                    "{label}: traced repository path resolves into forbidden data"
  7673	                );
  7674	            }
  7675	        }
  7676	        if lexical_lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  7677	            || lexical_lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  7678	            || lower.contains("/fuzz/corpus/")
  7679	            || lower.starts_with("fuzz/corpus/")
  7680	        {
  7681	            resolved.insert(format!("{lexical}\0{relative}"));
  7682	        }
  7683	    }
  7684	    if access == CorpusAccess::Required {
  7685	        anyhow::ensure!(
  7686	            !resolved.is_empty(),
  7687	            "{label}: trace contains no resolvable fuzz corpus path"
  7688	        );
  7689	    }
  7690	    let resolved = resolved.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
  7691	    let resolved_bytes = format!("{}\n", resolved.join("\n"));
  7692	    Ok(blake3::hash(resolved_bytes.as_bytes()).to_hex().to_string())
  7693	}

  7695	/// Canonicalize the existing prefix of a traced path, then append historical
  7696	/// leaf components that libFuzzer may have deleted after opening them. This
  7697	/// preserves symlink and root-boundary checks without requiring every path in
  7698	/// a long-running trace to remain present at receipt time.
  7699	fn canonicalize_trace_path(path: &Path) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
  7700	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
  7701	    let mut cursor = path;
  7702	    loop {
  7703	        match fs::symlink_metadata(cursor) {
  7704	            Ok(_) => break,
  7705	            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
  7706	                missing.push(
  7707	                    cursor
  7708	                        .file_name()
  7709	                        .context("traced path has no recoverable leaf")?
  7710	                        .to_owned(),
  7711	                );
  7712	                let leaf = missing.last().expect("just pushed missing leaf");
  7713	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7714	                    leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".") && leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".."),
  7715	                    "traced path contains a parent-directory suffix"
  7716	                );
  7717	                cursor = cursor
  7718	                    .parent()
  7719	                    .context("traced path has no existing ancestor")?;
  7720	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7721	                    cursor.file_name() != Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("corpus")),
  7722	                    "traced path is missing a corpus entry; symlink history is unavailable"
  7723	                );
  7724	            }
  7725	            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
  7726	        }
  7727	    }
  7728	    let mut canonical = fs::canonicalize(cursor)?;
  7729	    for component in missing.into_iter().rev() {
  7730	        canonical.push(component);
  7731	    }
  7732	    Ok(canonical)
  7733	}

  7735	fn trace_path_to_repo(root: &Utf8Path, trace_root: &Path, lexical: &str) -> Result<Utf8PathBuf> {

  7695	/// Canonicalize the existing prefix of a traced path, then append historical

  7698	/// a long-running trace to remain present at receipt time.
  7699	fn canonicalize_trace_path(path: &Path) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
  7700	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
  7701	    let mut cursor = path;
  7702	    loop {
  7703	        match fs::symlink_metadata(cursor) {
  7704	            Ok(_) => break,
  7705	            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
  7706	                missing.push(
  7707	                    cursor
  7708	                        .file_name()
  7709	                        .context("traced path has no recoverable leaf")?
  7710	                        .to_owned(),
  7711	                );
  7712	                let leaf = missing.last().expect("just pushed missing leaf");
  7713	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7714	                    leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".") && leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".."),
  7715	                    "traced path contains a parent-directory suffix"
  7716	                );
  7717	                cursor = cursor
  7718	                    .parent()
  7719	                    .context("traced path has no existing ancestor")?;
  7720	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7721	                    cursor.file_name() != Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("corpus")),
  7722	                    "traced path is missing a corpus entry; symlink history is unavailable"
  7723	                );
  7724	            }
  7725	            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
  7726	        }
  7727	    }
  7728	    let mut canonical = fs::canonicalize(cursor)?;
  7729	    for component in missing.into_iter().rev() {
  7730	        canonical.push(component);
  7731	    }
  7732	    Ok(canonical)

  7371	fn locked_corpus_write(
  7372	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7373	    candidates: &[String],
  7374	    label: &str,
  7375	) -> Result<Option<String>> {
  7376	    let canonical_root = fs::canonicalize(root.as_std_path())
  7377	        .with_context(|| format!("{label}: canonicalize repository root"))?;
  7378	    let identities = locked_corpus_identities(root, "conformance/corpora")?;
  7379	    for lexical in candidates {
  7380	        let path = Path::new(lexical);
  7381	        // Blind pass 1 at 78c8f9b (A12): a relative write from a subdirectory,
  7382	        // `../conformance/corpora/heldout/x`, joined onto the root climbed out
  7383	        // of it and passed. The cwd is not receipted, so a relative write that
  7384	        // names the locked corpus at all is refused, before any resolution.
  7385	        let lower = lexical.to_ascii_lowercase();
  7386	        if !path.is_absolute()
  7387	            && (lower.contains("conformance/corpora/") || lower.ends_with("conformance/corpora"))
  7388	        {
  7389	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  7390	        }
  7391	        let local = if path.is_absolute() {
  7392	            path.to_path_buf()
  7393	        } else {
  7394	            root.as_std_path().join(path)
  7395	        };
  7396	        // A path that no longer resolves (deleted after the trace) is judged
  7397	        // lexically: the conservative direction, since a lexical
  7398	        // conformance/corpora prefix still refuses.
  7399	        let canonical = canonicalize_trace_path(&local).unwrap_or(local);
  7400	        if let Ok(relative) = canonical.strip_prefix(&canonical_root)
  7401	            && relative
  7402	                .to_string_lossy()
  7403	                .to_ascii_lowercase()
  7404	                .starts_with("conformance/corpora")
  7405	        {
  7406	            return Ok(Some(lexical.clone()));
  7407	        }
  7408	        // A07: a hard link is a second name for the same inode, so no amount
  7409	        // of path reasoning sees it. Identity does.
  7410	        if let Ok(metadata) = fs::symlink_metadata(&canonical) {
  7411	            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
  7412	            if identities.contains(&(metadata.dev(), metadata.ino())) {
  7413	                return Ok(Some(format!(
  7414	                    "{lexical} (hard link into the locked corpus)"
  7415	                )));
  7416	            }
  7417	        }
  7418	    }
  7419	    Ok(None)
  7420	}

  7633	    root: &Utf8Path,
  7634	    trace_root: &str,
  7635	    open_paths: &BTreeSet<String>,

  7695	/// Canonicalize the existing prefix of a traced path, then append historical
  7696	/// leaf components that libFuzzer may have deleted after opening them. This
  7697	/// preserves symlink and root-boundary checks without requiring every path in
  7698	/// a long-running trace to remain present at receipt time.
  7699	fn canonicalize_trace_path(path: &Path) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
  7700	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
  7701	    let mut cursor = path;
  7702	    loop {
  7703	        match fs::symlink_metadata(cursor) {
  7704	            Ok(_) => break,
  7705	            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
  7706	                missing.push(
  7707	                    cursor
  7708	                        .file_name()
  7709	                        .context("traced path has no recoverable leaf")?
  7710	                        .to_owned(),
  7711	                );
  7712	                let leaf = missing.last().expect("just pushed missing leaf");
  7713	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7714	                    leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".") && leaf != std::ffi::OsStr::new(".."),
  7715	                    "traced path contains a parent-directory suffix"
  7716	                );
  7717	                cursor = cursor
  7718	                    .parent()
  7719	                    .context("traced path has no existing ancestor")?;
  7720	                anyhow::ensure!(
  7721	                    cursor.file_name() != Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new("corpus")),
  7722	                    "traced path is missing a corpus entry; symlink history is unavailable"
  7723	                );
  7724	            }
  7725	            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
  7726	        }
  7727	    }
  7728	    let mut canonical = fs::canonicalize(cursor)?;
  7729	    for component in missing.into_iter().rev() {
  7730	        canonical.push(component);
  7731	    }
  7732	    Ok(canonical)
  7733	}

  5329	fn collect_runnable_test_functions(text: &str, names: &mut BTreeMap<String, usize>) {
  5330	    let mut test_pending = false;
  5331	    let mut excluded = false;
  5332	    for line in text.lines() {
  5333	        let trimmed = line.trim();
  5334	        if trimmed.starts_with("#[test]") {
  5335	            test_pending = true;
  5336	        } else if trimmed.starts_with("#[ignore")
  5337	            || (trimmed.starts_with("#[cfg_attr(") && trimmed.contains("ignore"))
  5338	            || cfg_attribute_excludes(trimmed)
  5339	        {
  5340	            // Keep an exclusion only across the attribute list immediately
  5341	            // preceding one test. A module-level cfg or one ignored function
  5342	            // must not poison every later runnable test in the file.
  5343	            excluded = true;
  5344	        } else if test_pending {
  5345	            let declaration = trimmed.strip_prefix("pub ").unwrap_or(trimmed);
  5346	            let declaration = declaration.strip_prefix("async ").unwrap_or(declaration);
  5347	            if let Some(rest) = declaration.strip_prefix("fn ") {
  5348	                if let Some(name) = rest
  5349	                    .split('(')
  5350	                    .next()
  5351	                    .filter(|name| !name.trim().is_empty())
  5352	                    && !excluded
  5353	                {
  5354	                    *names.entry(name.trim().to_owned()).or_default() += 1;
  5355	                }
  5356	                test_pending = false;
  5357	                excluded = false;
  5358	            }
  5359	        } else if !test_pending {
  5360	            // An attribute that did not lead directly to a test belongs to a
  5361	            // module/helper declaration, not to the next test function.
  5362	            excluded = false;
  5363	        }
  5364	    }
  5365	}

  5367	fn cfg_attribute_excludes(trimmed: &str) -> bool {
  5368	    if !trimmed.starts_with("#[cfg(") {
  5369	        return false;
  5370	    }
  5371	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(any())]" {
  5372	        return true;
  5373	    }
  5374	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(test)]" {
  5375	        return false;
  5376	    }
  5377	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(not(test))]" {
  5378	        return true;
  5379	    }
  5380	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(unix)]" {
  5381	        return !cfg!(unix);
  5382	    }
  5383	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(windows)]" {
  5384	        return !cfg!(windows);
  5385	    }
  5386	    if trimmed.contains("target_os = \"linux\"") {
  5387	        return !cfg!(target_os = "linux");
  5388	    }
  5389	    if trimmed.contains("target_os = \"windows\"") {
  5390	        return !cfg!(target_os = "windows");
  5391	    }
  5392	    // Unknown predicates remain fail-closed: scanner cannot prove they are
  5393	    // active on this host.
  5394	    true
  5395	}

 12774	/// Replace one retained sanitizer binary's runtime marker with inert bytes and
 12775	/// invoke the same compiler/runtime proof verifier used by qualification. This
 12776	/// keeps C27 tied to an executable artifact attack, not an in-memory boolean.
 12777	fn run_sanitizer_canary(root: &Utf8Path) -> Result<()> {
 12778	    let path = root.join("conformance/haqp/evidence/fuzz.json");
 12779	    let rows: Vec<FuzzEvidence> = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path)?)?;
 12780	    let row = rows
 12781	        .iter()
 12782	        .find(|row| row.sanitizer_proof.is_some())
 12783	        .context("sanitizer canary requires retained sanitizer proof")?;
 12784	    let mut proof = row
 12785	        .sanitizer_proof
 12786	        .clone()
 12787	        .context("sanitizer canary requires retained sanitizer proof")?;
 12788	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-sanitizer-canary")?;
 12789	    let scratch_root = scratch.path();
 12790	    // ScratchDir is fresh and private to this canary. Reject path escapes
 12791	    // before reading committed artifacts or creating any scratch entry.
 12792	    for (path, label) in [
 12793	        (&proof.binary, "sanitizer canary binary"),
 12794	        (&proof.runtime_probe, "sanitizer canary probe"),
 12795	        (&proof.build_log, "sanitizer canary build log"),
 12796	    ] {
 12797	        let candidate = Utf8Path::new(path);
 12798	        anyhow::ensure!(
 12799	            !candidate.is_absolute()
 12800	                && !candidate
 12801	                    .components()
 12802	                    .any(|part| part == camino::Utf8Component::ParentDir)
 12803	                && !is_locked_acceptance_path(path),
 12804	            "{label} path {path:?} escapes scratch evidence root"
 12805	        );
 12806	    }
 12807	    let binary_path = safe_repo_path(root, &proof.binary, "sanitizer canary binary")?;
 12808	    let mut binary = fs::read(&binary_path)?;
 12809	    let marker = match row.sanitizer.as_str() {
 12810	        "address" | "leak" => b"asan_globals".as_slice(),
 12811	        "memory" => b"msan".as_slice(),
 12812	        "thread" => b"tsan".as_slice(),
 12813	        _ => anyhow::bail!("unsupported sanitizer {}", row.sanitizer),
 12814	    };
 12815	    let mut replaced = false;
 12816	    for offset in 0..=binary.len().saturating_sub(marker.len()) {
 12817	        if &binary[offset..offset + marker.len()] == marker {
 12818	            binary[offset..offset + marker.len()].fill(b'X');
 12819	            replaced = true;
 12820	        }
 12821	    }
 12822	    anyhow::ensure!(
 12823	        replaced,
 12824	        "sanitizer canary source binary has no runtime marker"
 12825	    );
 12826	    let scratch_binary_path = scratch_root.join(&proof.binary);
 12827	    let scratch_probe_path = scratch_root.join(&proof.runtime_probe);
 12828	    let scratch_log_path = scratch_root.join(&proof.build_log);
 12829	    fs::create_dir_all(scratch_binary_path.parent().expect("binary parent"))?;
 12830	    fs::create_dir_all(scratch_probe_path.parent().expect("probe parent"))?;
 12831	    fs::create_dir_all(scratch_log_path.parent().expect("log parent"))?;
 12832	    fs::write(&scratch_binary_path, &binary)?;
 12833	    let runtime_probe_path = safe_repo_path(root, &proof.runtime_probe, "sanitizer canary probe")?;
 12834	    let build_log_path = safe_repo_path(root, &proof.build_log, "sanitizer canary build log")?;
 12835	    fs::copy(runtime_probe_path, &scratch_probe_path)?;
 12836	    fs::copy(build_log_path, &scratch_log_path)?;
 12837	    proof.binary_blake3 = hex_digest(&binary);
 12838	    proof.runtime_probe_blake3 = hex_digest(&fs::read(&scratch_probe_path)?);
 12839	    proof.build_log_blake3 = hex_digest(&fs::read(&scratch_log_path)?);
 12840	    let error = verify_sanitizer_proof(scratch_root, row, &proof, None)
 12841	        .expect_err("uninstrumented sanitizer canary must fail closed");
 12842	    anyhow::bail!("sanitizer proof lacks compiler/runtime replay: {error}");
 12843	}

  4052	/// The killing tests AM-17.10 derives for `mutant`: the candidates are the
  4053	/// tests the packet maps to its requirement, in packet order; the primary is
  4054	/// the first candidate observed the way this operator shows itself; the
  4055	/// secondary is the first remaining candidate of a different evidence kind.
  4056	/// Each fallback is to the next candidate, never outside the requirement.
  4057	fn derive_killing_tests(packet: &Packet, mutant: &Mutant) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
  4058	    // Position among the mutants sharing this requirement. F-05 caps any one
  4059	    // test at a quarter of the plan, and a rule that always picked the first
  4060	    // apt candidate put P1-T07 on 46% of it. Rotation spreads the claim across
  4061	    // the tests that defend the requirement instead of piling it on the first.
  4062	    let ordinal = packet
  4063	        .mutants
  4064	        .iter()
  4065	        .take_while(|other| other.id != mutant.id)
  4066	        .filter(|other| other.requirement == mutant.requirement)
  4067	        .count();
