  4069	        .iter()
  4070	        .find(|(operator, _)| *operator == mutant.operator)
  4071	        .map(|(_, kind)| *kind)
  4072	        .with_context(|| {
  4073	            format!(
  4074	                "{} carries operator {:?}, which names no observation kind; AM-17.10 requires \
  4075	                 one before the plan can carry the operator",
  4076	                mutant.id, mutant.operator
  4077	            )
  4078	        })?;

  4080	        .tests
  4081	        .iter()
  4082	        .filter(|test| test.requirements.contains(&mutant.requirement))
  4083	        .collect();

  4085	        candidates.len() >= 2,
  4086	        "{} names requirement {}, which {} test(s) defend; a pair of killers needs two",
  4087	        mutant.id,
  4088	        mutant.requirement,
  4089	        candidates.len()
  4090	    );

  4092	        .iter()
  4093	        .filter(|test| test.evidence.iter().any(|kind| kind == observed))
  4094	        .collect();

  4096	    // fallback candidate list is still a list, and taking its head every time
  4097	    // is what put one test on 46% of the plan (review of `95a97b8b`).
  4098	    let primary = if observed_candidates.is_empty() {
  4099	        candidates[ordinal % candidates.len()]

  4101	        observed_candidates[ordinal % observed_candidates.len()]
  4102	    };

  4104	        .iter()
  4105	        .position(|test| test.id == primary.id)
  4106	        .context("the primary is one of the candidates")?;

  4108	    let secondary = (1..candidates.len())
  4109	        .map(after)
  4110	        .find(|test| test.evidence != primary.evidence)
  4111	        .unwrap_or_else(|| after(1));

  4137	/// Whether `coordinate` — a `file:line` a finding names — points at a line

  4139	/// decides whether a finding is fixed or recorded is evidence rather than the

  4141	pub fn coordinate_is_campaign_churn(root: &Utf8Path, coordinate: &str) -> Result<bool> {

  4143	        .rsplit_once(':')
  4144	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} is not a file:line coordinate"))?;
  4145	    let line: u32 = line
  4146	        .parse()
  4147	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} does not name a line"))?;
  4148	    anyhow::ensure!(line > 0, "{coordinate:?} names line zero");

  4150	        root,
  4151	        &[
  4152	            "blame",
  4153	            "--porcelain",
  4154	            "-L",
  4155	            &format!("{line},{line}"),
  4156	            "--",
  4157	            file,
  4158	        ],
  4159	    )
  4160	    .with_context(|| format!("blame {coordinate}"))?;
  4161	    let commit = blamed
  4162	        .split_whitespace()
  4163	        .next()
  4164	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate}: blame named no commit"))?;

  4167	    // line was written during the campaign.
  4168	    let status = Command::new("git")
  4169	        .current_dir(root)
  4170	        .args(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", CAMPAIGN_FIRST_LANE, commit])

  5341	            // preceding one test. A module-level cfg or one ignored function
  5342	            // must not poison every later runnable test in the file.

  5346	            let declaration = declaration.strip_prefix("async ").unwrap_or(declaration);
  5347	            if let Some(rest) = declaration.strip_prefix("fn ") {
  5348	                if let Some(name) = rest

  5350	                    .next()

  5374	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(test)]" {

  5377	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(not(test))]" {

  5381	        return !cfg!(unix);

  5383	    if trimmed == "#[cfg(windows)]" {

 10711	fn verify_fuzz_budget(declared: &[Generated], recorded: &[FuzzEvidence]) -> Result<()> {
 10712	    let elapsed_seconds: BTreeMap<&str, u64> = recorded
 10713	        .iter()
 10714	        .map(|row| (row.target.as_str(), row.elapsed_s))
 10715	        .collect();
 10716	    let mut total_minutes = 0_u64;
 10717	    for family in declared {
 10718	        if family.result != "pass" {
 10719	            continue;
 10720	        }
 10721	        if family.fuzz_targets.is_empty() {
 10722	            anyhow::bail!(
 10723	                "{} claims pass but names no fuzz target; ADR-0020 §4 gives every \
 10724	                 family its own sanitizer campaign, and a family with no target \
 10725	                 has had none",

 10727	            );
 10728	        }

 10733	                    "{} names fuzz target {target:?}, which the committed campaign did not run",

 12454	/// Run one canary per DECLARED row, and require each row's prose to describe
 12455	/// the mutation that was actually performed (M17.5 pass-2 #22).
 12456	///
 12457	/// The runner used to iterate a hardcoded canary range and read only
 12458	/// `expected_failure`. `Canary.gate` and `Canary.violation` were therefore
 12459	/// decorative: the packet could say C09 relabels a mutation family while the
 12460	/// executed arm did something entirely different, and nothing would notice.
 12461	/// That matters because the canary table is the artifact a reader trusts to
 12462	/// learn WHAT the canaries prove — unverified prose in that position is
 12463	/// worse than no prose, because it reads as evidence.
 12464	///
 12465	/// Driving the loop from `packet.canaries` rather than a hardcoded `1..=16`
 12466	/// closes a drift hazard rather than a live hole: `verify_canary_inventory`
 12467	/// currently pins the id set to exactly C01–C25, so an extra row is rejected
 12468	/// before it reaches this function. But that rule is the only thing keeping the
 12469	/// hardcoded range honest, and the natural future edit — relaxing it to a
 12470	/// minimum when canary 17 is written — would have left the new canaries
 12471	/// declared, counted, and never executed. The loop now cannot disagree with the
 12472	/// table it reports on.
 12473	fn run_canary_suite(
 12474	    root: &Utf8Path,
 12475	    baseline: &Packet,
 12476	    markdown: &str,
 12477	) -> Result<Vec<CanaryEvidence>> {
 12478	    let baseline_digest = packet_digest(baseline)?;
 12479	    let mut records = Vec::new();
 12480	    for row in &baseline.canaries {
 12481	        let mut packet = baseline.clone();
 12482	        let mut altered_markdown = markdown.to_owned();
 12483	        let performed = mutate_canary(
 12484	            &row.id,
 12485	            &mut packet,
 12486	            &mut altered_markdown,
 12487	            &baseline_digest,
 12488	        )?;
 12489	        require_eq(
 12490	            &format!("{}.violation (packet prose vs executed mutation)", row.id),
 12491	            &row.violation,
 12492	            performed,
 12493	        )?;
 12494	        let observed = if is_qualification_canary(&row.id) {
 12495	            run_qualification_canary(root, baseline, &row.id)
 12496	                .expect_err("qualification canary must fail closed")
 12497	                .to_string()
 12498	        } else {
 12499	            verify_packet_shape(&packet)
 12500	                .and_then(|()| verify_packet_statuses(&packet, inventory_statuses()))
 12501	                .and_then(|()| verify_markdown_surface_text(&altered_markdown, &packet))
 12502	                .expect_err("mutated canary must fail closed")
 12503	                .to_string()
 12504	        };
 12505	        if !canary_failure_matches(&row.expected_failure, &observed) {
 12506	            anyhow::bail!(
 12507	                "{}: expected failure {:?}, observed {observed:?}",
 12508	                row.id,
 12509	                row.expected_failure
 12510	            );
 12511	        }
 12512	        let canonical = canary_expected_prefix(&row.id)?;
 12513	        if let Some((_, phrase)) = CANARY_REQUIRED_PHRASE
 12514	            .iter()
 12515	            .find(|(id, _)| *id == row.id.as_str())
 12516	        {
 12517	            anyhow::ensure!(
 12518	                row.expected_failure.contains(phrase),
 12519	                "{}: expected failure {:?} must name the violation this canary performs \
 12520	                 ({phrase:?}); its prefix is shared by every refusal of its kind",
 12521	                row.id,
 12522	                row.expected_failure
 12523	            );
 12524	        }
 12525	        anyhow::ensure!(
 12526	            row.expected_failure.starts_with(canonical),
 12527	            "{}: expected failure {:?} is outside closed canary failure registry {:?}",
 12528	            row.id,
 12529	            row.expected_failure,
 12530	            canonical
 12531	        );
 12532	        records.push(CanaryEvidence {
 12533	            id: row.id.clone(),
 12534	            gate: row.gate.clone(),
 12535	            violation: row.violation.clone(),
 12536	            expected_failure: row.expected_failure.clone(),
 12537	            observed_failure: observed,
 12538	            caught: true,
 12539	            mutation_semantics: canary_mutation_semantics(&row.id)?.to_owned(),
 12540	        });
 12541	    }
 12542	    Ok(records)
 12543	}
